purpose: Every important thought from the unsolved.md work, written the moment it is thought, so an agent that runs out of usage mid-task loses nothing. RULE (owner, 2026-11-14): every agent working the loop — fable, argon, the deepseek lanes — appends a thought entry HERE the moment the thought occurs, BEFORE proving anything, not in a batch at the end. One entry per realisation: what you noticed, what you suspect, what you are about to try. Append-only, newest last. Read THIS FILE FIRST on resume.

schema.at: ISO 8601 local time the entry was written
schema.by: agent that wrote it (fable-5.2, deepseek-v4.1-flash, argon, human)
schema.item: the construct or task, one line
schema.thought: what the writer is considering or has just realised - write it here the moment it occurs, before proving anything
schema.finding: what is actually true, in plain words
schema.evidence: reproduction path and the numbers that prove it, or null when it is still a thought

resume.build: export PATH=$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH; cd /tmp/rg-fable-wt && CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/rg-fable-target cargo build --release --target x86_64-unknown-linux-musl --features "deep parser"
resume.tests: CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/rg-fable-test cargo test  (then again with --features "deep parser")
resume.rule: Append an entry the moment a thought matters: which construct you are about to test and why, which reader you suspect, which file you are about to change, what the last measurement showed. kind=thought, status=thinking, no evidence yet - that is fine. Never batch to the end of a run: the account can cut you off at any tool call and anything not in this file or in a commit is lost. When a thought becomes a finding, append a new entry with the evidence and leave the thought where it is.

entries.item: js corpus is a random sample of every .js under both home trees
entries.finding: A large share of the js corpus was built output - webpack chunks, .next/static, dist, .min.js. Each is one enormous line, so per-line pairing has nothing to compare and its losses are noise no reader fix can remove. That is why js had been stuck at a low file count with high losses.
entries.evidence: old sample /tmp/opencode/sweep-local/js-minified-baseline: 96/1995 files, 164 losses. New source-only sample: 149/2000 files, 270 losses - fewer files pass because they contain constructs. Filter: /tmp/opencode/js-source-filter.py (>=15 lines, no line >400 chars, built dirs excluded); sweep-local.sh pipes through it.

entries.item: class field with a computed key: `static [entityKind] = "x"`
entries.finding: The lexer named the target `static` because unpack_targets only stripped const/let/var/my/our/local/val/mut; a class-field modifier is not a binding. The CST names the computed key, which is right.
entries.evidence: /tmp/js-static/a.js (4 lines): 1 loss -> 0. js 149/270 -> 138/244, ts 91/114 -> 84/107, python and rust held.

entries.item: rust method call after a block-like operand: `async { s }.boxed()`
entries.finding: After a block-like operand in statement position the grammar writes `.name(args)` as one field_expression carrying its own arguments, so no call_expression exists to read and the call left the record. Treating a field_expression with an arguments child as a call repairs it.
entries.evidence: src/deep_facts/rust.rs: rust_block_method + rust_call/rust_callee. Measured by deepseek-v4.1-flash in /tmp/rg-fable-wt: rust 260/1816 (287) -> 255/1816 (282); js, ts, python untouched.

entries.item: js for-header assignment emits an event the CST does not have
entries.finding: For `for (i = length; i-- !== 0;)` the lexer emits an `a` event with targets [i]; the CST emits nothing on that line because it records a for header's binder in the statement's target list. Suspect double accounting on the lexer side, but not yet confirmed against pipeline.rs.
entries.evidence: /tmp/js-for/a.js reproduces 2 losses (lines 17 and 32); the corpus shows 11 rows, but only about 2 distinct files.

entries.item: corpus duplication inflates every corpus, worst in rust
entries.finding: Measured by content hash: js 2000 files / 1854 unique (7% dup), ts 2000 / 1537 (23%), rust 1816 / 1000 (45%). The rust corpus is every .rs in the workspace, which now holds many near-identical worktrees, so almost half the rust losses are the same code counted again. Dedupe would reset every rust baseline - owner decision, not a lane decision.
entries.evidence: sha256 over each corpus directory, 2026-11-14.

entries.item: usage limit stopped the run mid-task
entries.finding: Fable 5.2 hit its 5-hour limit at 12:36 EST, resets 17:10 (America/New_York). It had applied the rust field_expression fix but not committed it. Its measurement helpers and reproductions are in /tmp/fable-m/tools and /tmp/fable-r.
entries.evidence: session 4bacd5d1-85a3-4e2c-9a91-c8453e069d67.jsonl, last assistant message.

entries.item: js corpus carried duplicate content
entries.finding: The 2000-file js sample held 146 files that were byte-identical to another file in the sample (webpack copies of one library across build dirs). Every such file counted as its own fallback, so one construct moved the js number several times over.
entries.evidence: sha256 over the sample: 2000 files, 1854 unique. After dropping the duplicates the same binary reads js 125/1854 (223) instead of 138/2000 (244) - 13 files and 21 losses were pure duplicates. tools/js_source_filter.py now drops repeats by content hash during collection.

entries.item: ts `{} as Record<string, number>`: the type after `as` is not a value
entries.finding: `as` is already noise, so the lexer skipped the keyword but then read the type like an expression: the value of `const total = {} as Record<string, number>` came out as the type argument tuple, while the CST writes only the cast value `{}`.
entries.evidence: /tmp/ts-as/a.ts (4 lines): 2 losses -> 0 under both readers. Fixed by skipping the type expression after `as` in TS/TSX (Emit::skip_type: runs to the first token that cannot continue a type at depth zero). ts 84/2000 (107) -> 82/2000 (101); js, python and rust unchanged.

entries.item: ts declaration classes with multi-line type-parameter lists
entries.thought: 16 rows, all in declaration files (types.d.ts, index.ts declare class). A one-line signature in a class body is already suppressed, so the shape that breaks must be the type-parameter list that spans lines: `$$eval<` newline `Selector extends string,` newline `>(…): Promise<…>;`. The type parameters look like a group the statement never closes, so the class frame never opens and the members are read as module-level statements - my 2-file reproduction emits both signatures at `a.ts:<module>`. Cheapest next probe: check whether an unmatched `<` is what keeps the statement alive across those lines, before writing any rule.
entries.evidence: /tmp/ts-decl2/a.ts: 2 losses, both `no event on a line both readers can mean` at module level; /tmp/ts-c1 and /tmp/ts-c2 (one-line signatures, with and without `declare`) have 0 losses, so length is the trigger.

entries.item: js for-header events: extra lexer events are tolerated, so the 14 rows are pairing noise
entries.thought: /tmp/js-for3/a.js compares `for (i = 0; …)` against `for (var j = 0; …)`: the lexer emits an extra `x` (the condition merge) on both header lines and the CST emits neither, yet the file measures 0 losses. So a lone extra header event is not itself a loss - the corpus rows come from somewhere else (a line the CST attributes differently), and chasing them from the header side would be guessing. Leave this cluster alone until a reproduction shows a real disagreement.
entries.evidence: /tmp/js-for3: lexer x+body vs deep body on lines 3 and 4, losses 0. Corpus rows: 000399_index.js:82, 000995_natural.js:63/67/75, 001055_index.js:105.

entries.item: rust was skipping JavaScript and Python keywords as if they were its own
entries.finding: The generic NOISE list is a mix of JS, Python and Perl operators, and Rust went through it with only `new` excepted. So a Rust variable named `lambda`, `is`, `and`, `or`, `var`, `my`, `our`, `then`, `of`, `do` or `local` was skipped as if it were a keyword, and the value lost the name the CST writes (`self.line(lambda)` came out as a call whose argument was the constant 0).
entries.evidence: /tmp/rgn-lam/a.rs (7 lines): 1 loss -> 0. Fix: a Rust-only RS_NOISE list holding just the words that really are Rust keywords (await, yield, async, in, as, if, else, for, return, let, const, mut, ref, unsafe, pub, move). Measured: rust 255/1816 (282) -> 246/1816 (267); js, ts and python unchanged.

entries.item: ts nested type arguments with a comma break the statement, not the type parameters
entries.thought: Correction to my earlier note. A one-line generic signature is fine (`first<T>`, `first<T = unknown>`, `first<T extends unknown>` all measure 0 losses), and a multi-line type-parameter list without a nested comma is fine too. What breaks is a nested type argument carrying a COMMA: `first<T = Record<string, unknown>>(): Promise<T | null>;` inside `declare class D` emits at `<module>` instead of opening the class frame - one loss. So the trigger is the comma inside `<…>` being taken as a statement separator because the angle brackets are not bracket depth for the splitter. That is the thing to fix, and it is a general type-argument scanner, not a class-member rule.
entries.evidence: /tmp/ts-b1/a.ts 1 loss; /tmp/ts-b2/{a,b,c}.ts 0 losses.

entries.item: rust: a turbofish inside a call argument breaks the whole argument list
entries.thought: loss_shapes on all four corpora this hour: rust 267 over 244 files (223 empty-scope, then t: m:, m: m:, m: n:assert_eq 7 each), ts 101 over 64 (t: m: 16, t: n:never 7), js 223 over 125 (empty 42, then 0 8, m: m: 7, c(0; m: 7), python 18 over 14 (empty 5, n:Exception 2). The rust assert_eq rows all carry `Vec::<T>::new()` as an argument.
entries.finding: `assert_eq!(no_fill.iterate(), Vec::<MatchAction>::new())` loses the row: the lexer writes `m:[n:assert_eq,m:[c(n:no_fill;[0]),n:Vec,m:[n:new,0]]]` where the CST has `t:[c(n:no_fill;[]),c(n:Vec;[])]`. The turbofish skip in `chain` consumes `::<...>` but the callee the CST keeps for `Vec::<T>::new()` is `Vec`, and the argument list collapses (both args of side_tab_page merged into one `m`), so the failure is in the call-argument split around the turbofish, not in the chain. Repro: /tmp/rgn-turbo/a.rs, 1 loss.
entries.evidence: /tmp/rgn-turbo/a.rs 1 loss; got vs want in the entry above; 7 rows in the rust corpus (001162/001316 matching_core.rs:245, 001548 integrity_tests.rs:138/142/150, 001607 static_flush.rs:37, 001626 side_accent_radius.rs:124).

entries.item: ts: a defaulted type parameter closing as >> lost the class member's colon
entries.thought: The class frame was never the problem. `member_type_cut` counts `<` as depth and `>` as its closer, but the lexer emits `>>` as ONE op token, so `f<T = Record<string, unknown>>(): void` kept depth 2 at the colon, the cut was never found, and the member fell through to expression_event -- which is why the event carried the whole merged value.
entries.finding: Fix: `>>` and `>>>` decrement by 2 and 3 in member_type_cut. The four bracketing repros go to 0 losses (/tmp/ts-b1, /tmp/ts-m, /tmp/ts-m2, /tmp/ts-m3); ts 82/2000 (101) -> 80/2000 (89), js 125/223, python 14/18, rust 246/267 unchanged. Both cargo suites green.
entries.evidence: /tmp/ts-b1/a.ts 1 loss -> 0 with no flows at all (a signature writes nothing, which is what the CST does); tools/loss_count.py after the fix: ts 80/2000 (89).

entries.item: ts multi-line type parameter lists still emit at module level
entries.thought: /tmp/ts-decl2/a.ts still loses 1 after d0afd80: a member whose `<` opens at the end of one line and closes several lines later (`$$eval<` newline `Selector extends string,` ...). on_newline() only refuses to split when self.brackets is non-empty, and `<` never enters self.brackets. inside_type_arguments() already exists and is consulted by the comma rule, so the same guard belongs in on_newline -- but it must not swallow a real comparison (`a < b` at end of line), so it needs the `<` to be an opener in a declaration position, not any `<`.
entries.evidence: RG_LOSSES=1 on /tmp/ts-decl2 after the fix: 1 loss, 'event x line 3 ... wanted line 3 value t:[m:[n:$$eval,...'

entries.item: ts multi-line type parameter list: on_newline guard attempt failed
entries.thought: Tried the guard the note called for: in TS/TSX, do not end a statement at a newline when the line ends in `<` preceded by a name. Reverted.
entries.finding: The repro /tmp/ts-decl2 still loses 1 with the guard in place, so the split is not happening at the newline after `<`. The member is still emitted at module level, which means either the statement is closed elsewhere (the comma rules already skip inside_type_arguments) or the class frame is not the frame being used. Not worth a second guess without a debug build; the next attempt should instrument the statement boundary rather than pattern-match.
entries.evidence: built with the guard (2m24s), /tmp/ts-decl2 losses=1 (unchanged), /tmp/ts-b1 and /tmp/ts-m still 0. Patch reverted with git checkout.

entries.item: js: the deep reader writes a constant for an identifier named async
entries.thought: loss_shapes on js put `c(n:env.stack;[m:[m:[n:value,n:value],...` at 7 rows: `env.stack.push({ value: value, dispose: dispose, async: async })`. I first patched expr.rs (the lexer's object-pair path) to collapse `k: k` shorthand - that made the LEXER wrong for all pairs and I reverted it (`git checkout`). The flows show the lexer is right and the deep reader is wrong.
entries.finding: /tmp/js-obj2 isolates it: `f({async: async})` is the only failing shape (`{x: async}`, `{async: 1}`, `{async}`, `{yield: yield}` all pass). --lexer writes `m:[n:async]`, --deep writes `0`. So the deep reader's value rendering treats an identifier named `async` as a keyword and emits the constant, in an object property value position. Fix belongs in deep_facts (go.rs value rendering), not in expr.rs.
entries.evidence: /tmp/js-obj2/{a,b,c,d,e}.js: only a.js loses 1. Flows: --lexer a.js:f [['x',2,['c',0,['n','env.stack'],[['m',[['n','value'],['n','dispose'],['n','async']]]]]]] vs --deep [['m',[['m',[['n','value'],['n','value']]],['m',[['n','dispose'],['n','dispose']]],0]]]. Corpus rows: 7 (000249_Frame.js:55 first).

entries.shape: object property value named `async` renders as 0 in the deep reader
entries.attempt: added "async" to the path_of leaf-name arm in src/deep_facts/go.rs, the same treatment get/set/static already get
entries.result: loss count unchanged, 1 before and 1 after. The value never reaches path_of, so some other function renders it and falls through to the 0 constant.
entries.next: trace the object-literal value child: candidate is form()/decl_value() hitting an unhandled kind, not a name lookup. Grep the 0-fallback in the value renderer next.

entries.item: rust if let condition
entries.thought: The lexer read the whole `if let` condition as an expression, so the pattern's `Some(` became a call the CST never records. Everything left of the binding `=` is a pattern, not a value.

entries.item: sweep comparability
entries.thought: Two binaries built from the same source give rust 244/267 vs 242/274; one binary run twice is identical. Every A/B must build both sides from the tree.

entries.item: rust let-chain `&& let`
entries.thought: The 15 `(empty) @ &&` losses are let-chains: the continuation line arrives as its own statement starting with `&&`, so the assignment path read the pattern and emitted a call. Stripping every `let … =` segment after `&&`/`||` fixes that, but the compare then shows deep=1 lexer=2: the CST renders the let_condition operand of a binary expression as the constant 0, so the call inside `&& let Some(x) = g()` is genuinely missing from the deep record. The CST is the wrong reader here, not the lexer.

entries.item: js `{ async: async }`
entries.thought: Narrowed to a pair whose key and value are the same keyword: both children are layout, so the pair held nothing and rendered 0 while the lexer wrote the name once. Fixed in the pair arm of deep_facts (empty items -> one name when every word child is the same). js 117 files/211 losses -> 111/208; 6 clean, 0 new, 1 worse (000608_decorators.js 1->4, pairing shift).

entries.item: js `for (; cond;)` with a bare try body
entries.thought: Delta-reduced to 4 lines. The lexer writes the header condition, the CST drops it (the for_statement arm computes and discards every child after the second semicolon). With a block body the guard accepts the difference; with a bare try it reports four losses. I could not find why the tolerance differs, and making the lexer emit the condition broke two shapes that were clean. Not solved, written to unsolved.md for fable/argon.

entries.item: rust `impl Trait for Generic<T>`
entries.thought: The 14 `(empty) @ impl` losses were not a header event: the deep reader named the impl after the LAST identifier in the type, so `for JsonString<LogEntry>` became `LogEntry` while the lexer wrote `JsonString`. rust_type_name now takes the constructor for generic_type; scoped paths and references keep last_name. rust 204/233 -> 199/228.

entries.item: rust raw string `r"\\?\"` swallowed the rest of the file
entries.finding: The lexer handled `r#"..."#` but not a bare `r"..."`: it fell into the escaped-string path, where `\\` then `\"` ate the closing quote and the literal ran to the next quote in the file, several lines later. Code after it was read as code, so a `linear-gradient(` inside a CSS string became a call on three corpus files.
entries.evidence: /tmp/rs3/a.rs (4 lines): 1 loss -> 0. rust 190/220 -> 187/217 at this commit, js/ts/python held. Second loss family in the same files was the same cause.

entries.item: rust constructor pattern spanning lines recorded as a call
entries.finding: `if let Some(A::B(` ... `)) = value` is one statement in the lexer (the pattern's own `)` closes the bracket depth, so the `=` rides the same statement and it is read as an assignment whose target is the pattern). guard's is_pattern_call was single-line only. A wide variant now reads to the matching `)` and accepts only an arrow, a binding `=`, or a guard ending in an arrow before any `;`.
entries.evidence: /tmp/rp4 (001101_workflow_tests.rs, single file) 1 loss -> 0. rust files 194->190 at this step alone; whole-corpus measure after both: rust 177/211 (before the rebase onto 7b5e98c).

entries.item: js/rust symbol pairing matched a method to a same-named free function
entries.finding: The lexer stores a member as owner=`this` + name=`loadFile`; the CST stores one name `self.loadFile`. Neither pairing closure matched (names unequal), so the symbol fell through to the first same-*bare*-name row and compared a method's events against a free function twelve lines up. paired_name() now joins owner+name and normalises the `this.` receiver to `self.`; it also replaces the loose owner test, so two classes' same-named methods no longer cross-pair.
entries.evidence: /tmp/rj (001672_loader.js) 11 losses -> 0. js 108/205 -> 105/191, rust 187/177 files (217/211 losses) at that build; ts and python held. Whole-corpus after rebasing onto the let-else fix: js 105/191, ts 66/75, python 14/18, rust 158/191.

entries.item: python tuple assignment: `s, t = Counter(a), Counter(b)` had no var fact
entries.finding: Two halves. The CST read the tuple value as one expression, found no constructed class, and recorded no var at all; the lexer recorded one var but took the LAST target with the FIRST value's class (`send = RecvChannel` for `recv, send = RecvChannel(cid), SendChannel(cid)`). Neither fact is what the source says. CST now pairs target i with value i; the lexer does the same and names nothing when the two lists are the same length is false.
entries.evidence: /tmp/py1/a.py (3 lines): 1 loss -> 0. Four corpus files (000084_util, 000346_interpreters, 000515_subprocess, 000549_connection) 4 -> 0. python 14/18 -> 10/14; js, ts, rust held.

entries.item: python `some_b: 'B'` — a string annotation is a constant slot
entries.finding: The lexer writes `m:[n:some_b,0]` for a forward-reference annotation (name plus the constant the value reader gives a string); the CST's annotated arm dropped every part whose form was `0`, so the merge was one item short. The arm now keeps a string part even when its form is `0`.
entries.evidence: /tmp/px (000310_mod_generics_cache.py) 3 losses -> 0. python 10/14 -> 9/11; js, ts, rust unchanged.

entries.item: rust: the lexer names `loop`/`match` in a value, the CST does not
entries.finding: `let x = loop { … }` gives the lexer the value `m:[n:loop,m:[…]]`; the CST writes the block's merge only. A reserved word can never be a variable, so its absence from the CST's value is not a lost fact. covers_value now drops a missing `n:` atom that is a keyword for the file's language (is_keyword_callee, threaded through covers/covers_value/a_row_covers/type_as_target).
entries.evidence: RG_GUARD_DEBUG on /tmp/rx (001008_history_update.rs) shows missing=["n:loop"] and nothing else; after the change rust 158/191 -> 148/183, js/ts/python unchanged.

entries.item: js: `cond ? function a(){} : function b(){}` lost a constant slot
entries.finding: The lexer writes one `0` per branch it cannot name; the CST writes `0` for the first and the named function expression for the second, so the count of `0` atoms was short by one and the file fell back with 'a call or constant the lexer read is not in the CST value'. A `0` is the absence of a name, not a fact: the guard now accepts the count when the CST's value carries at least as many atoms as the lexer's. 8 of the 13 js files are 001898_output.js (var x = cond ? function(..) {…}).
entries.evidence: /tmp/jsT (001898_output.js): 7 losses -> 3. js 105/191 -> 92/165, rust 148/183 -> 142/177, ts and python held. The same shape is the ternary rows in ts (unchanged: their losses are elsewhere).

entries.item: rust: the lexer names an attributed item after its attribute (derive/case/cfg)
entries.finding: `#[rstest] #[case(1)] fn t() {…}` opens a lexer symbol `case` that owns the function body; `#[derive(..)] pub enum E { .. }` opens `derive`; `#[cfg(test)] mod tests {` opens `cfg` and never gives the module its owner. c_style_head read the attribute's `(` as the parameter list. Stripping the attribute fixes the names (rt6 and rt7 become clean, the `tests.` owner appears), but the count RISES: 141 -> 199 (open_block + c_style_head) and 141 -> 207 (c_style_head alone). Cause: the guard pairs a lexer symbol with a CST symbol by name and `continue`s when nothing pairs, so every event under a bogus `derive`/`case`/`cfg` symbol was never compared at all. Correct naming exposes ~60 real losses. The next fix is the guard (compare the events of an unpaired lexer symbol against the whole file's rows), not the lexer.
entries.evidence: /tmp/rt7 (a.rs `#[rstest] #[case(1)] fn t()`): baseline symbol `m.case`, patched `m.t`. /tmp/rt6 (001201_vr.rs): 4 losses baseline, 0 patched. Corpus: rust 114/141 baseline -> 164/199 with both edits -> 161/207 with c_style_head only. Both reverted with `git checkout -- src/parser.rs`.

entries.item: rust: a struct-literal receiver and a macro turbofish path lost their facts
entries.finding: Two CST-side losses fixed: `S { a: 1 }.into()` read the receiver as the path `S` and dropped every field (rust_callee now forms a struct_expression receiver), and inside a macro `Vec::<T>::new()` was recorded as a bare call `new` with no receiver while `crate::a::b` lost `crate` (rust_tt_value now keeps reading the path after the turbofish and rust_tt_path accepts the `crate`/`Self` nodes).
entries.evidence: /tmp/rt1 (struct receiver) and /tmp/rt4 (macro turbofish + crate path) both go from 1-2 losses to 0. Corpus: rust 126/160 -> 118/148 at the time, js/ts/python held.

entries.item: js/rust: a `for` header's init assignment and a tuple assignment had no CST event
entries.finding: `for (i = length; …)`: the CST only read the header after the first `;`, so the init expression was never read at all; `for_init` reads the pre-semicolon children (the grammar wraps them in an `expressions` node, so the assignment is one level down). In Rust `(a, b) = f()` is an `assignment_expression` whose left side is a `tuple_expression`, which `assignment_targets` did not map, so the event lost its targets. `let (mut a, mut b);` binds with no value: the lexer files a tuple value, the CST writes nothing, and `is_bare_let_line` accepts it.
entries.evidence: /tmp/jt1 + /tmp/jt2 (for init), /tmp/rtc + /tmp/rtd (tuple target, bare let) all go 1-3 losses -> 0. Corpus: js 92/165 -> 84/146 (with the x86 struct fix), rust 142/177 -> 134/169, then rust 107/124 -> 103/116 with the tuple target and bare let.

entries.item: guard: the rows of a definition's twin are the file's rows
entries.finding: The corpus copies whole modules, so a file can hold `fn f` twice. The pairing picked one twin (first match, or nearest line) and every event of the other was reported as absent. Two earlier attempts failed the rule: pairing by nearest line alone moved js 142 -> 155 and rust files 114 -> 117 (other twins paired wrongly). What works is additive: keep the pairing as it was and add every same-leaf-name deep symbol to the comparison pool, so a want can be covered by either twin.
entries.evidence: /tmp/rt6 (001201_vr.rs, `test_longer_period_requires_more_seed_inputs` at 320 and 363): 4 losses -> 0. Corpus at the time: js 80/142 -> 76/136, ts 65/73 -> 64/71, python 9/11 -> 8/8, rust 114/141 -> 108/126 (every corpus improved, so nothing was traded).

entries.item: rust target reached: 116 losses (owner's line is 120)
entries.finding: Rust is at 103/1816 files and 116 losses; js 70/1854 128, ts 63/2000 71, python 8/568 8. The remaining rust class is the multi-line expression: 39 of 116 are `no event on a line both readers can mean` where the lexer stamps a chain on its first line and the CST on the last (`self.0\n .insert(..)`, `/tmp/opencode/sweep-local/rust/000976_log_export.rs:176`). Widening the guard's one-line window is the only mechanical fix and it is exactly the window that stops a duplicate target on another line standing in for a missing event, so it stays unsolved on purpose.
entries.evidence: tools/loss_count.py after f1a9112: js 70/1854 128, ts 63/2000 71, python 8/568 8, rust 103/1816 116. tools/phase4_gate.py PASSED (js 70/150, ts 63/120, python 8 pinned, rust 103 pinned).

entries.item: final state: rust 107 losses (target 120), js 103, ts 43, python 8
entries.finding: After `fix(guard): a .d.ts member line declares no call` and the other lanes' `c3f0355`, tools/loss_count.py on c0b107e reads js 58/1854 103 losses, ts 55/2000 43, python 8/568 8, rust 93/1816 107. tools/phase4_gate.py PASSES with those numbers pinned and the construct record re-measured (rust 93). unsolved.md was rewritten to describe only the remaining classes: the multi-line expression (61 js / 14 ts / 12 rust), the rust `a name` families (match-arm nesting, turbofish in a struct literal, `if let` struct patterns, the constant-receiver call), the leading-dot shape fold over a constant receiver (12 rust), the attributed-item naming that the guard hides, `.d.ts` type expressions, the eight python rows, `this` in Rust, and corpus duplication. The enum-body class is gone: /tmp/rta/a.rs is clean on this tree.
entries.evidence: Final sweep: js 58/103, ts 55/43, python 8/8, rust 93/107. Note tools/loss_count.py exits non-zero on this tree with 'fewer losses than files' for ts (55 files, 43 losses): deep_losses can be 0 on a file that still falls back, so both columns are floors.
